hints: Resolve all three forces into horizontal ($x$) components: note the direction of each force relative to the axes.
Resolve all three forces into vertical ($y$) components.
Find resultant magnitude using $R = \sqrt{R_x^2 + R_y^2}$ and direction using $\tan\theta = \frac{R_y}{R_x}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve all forces along the positive $x$-axis using $\cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25}$ and $\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25}$:
$$R_x = 40\cos\alpha - 30\sin\alpha = 40\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) - 30\left(\frac{7}{25}\right) = \frac{960 - 210}{25} = \frac{750}{25} = 30\text{ N}$$

Resolve all forces along the positive $y$-axis:
$$R_y = 50 - 40\sin\alpha - 30\cos\alpha = 50 - 40\left(\frac{7}{25}\right) - 30\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) = 50 - \frac{280 + 720}{25} = 50 - 40 = 10\text{ N}$$

Calculate the magnitude of the resultant force $R$:
$$R = \sqrt{R_x^2 + R_y^2} = \sqrt{30^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{900 + 100} = \sqrt{1000} \approx 31.6\text{ N}$$

Find the angle $\theta$ that the resultant makes with the positive $x$-axis:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{R_y}{R_x} = \frac{10}{30} = \frac{1}{3} \implies \theta = \arctan\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \approx 18.4^\circ$$
The resultant force is $31.6\text{ N}$ acting at $18.4^\circ$ above the positive $x$-axis.

ai_rubric.Resolving Forces Along Chosen Axes: Uses resolve along the 40 N direction: $R_1=40-50(7/25)=26$.

teacher_walkthrough:
From $\tan\alpha = \frac{7}{24}$, use a 7-24-25 right-angled triangle to find the exact sine and cosine ratios:
$$\cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25} = 0.96,\quad \sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25} = 0.28$$

Resolve all forces horizontally along the positive $x$-axis. The 40 N force pulls to the right, and the 30 N force pulls to the left:
$$R_x = 40\cos\alpha - 30\sin\alpha$$

Substitute the trigonometric values into $R_x$ and evaluate the arithmetic:
$$R_x = 40(0.96) - 30(0.28) = 38.4 - 8.4 = 30\text{ N}$$

Resolve all forces vertically along the positive $y$-axis. The 50 N force pulls upward, while both the 40 N and 30 N forces pull downward:
$$R_y = 50 - 40\sin\alpha - 30\cos\alpha$$

Substitute the trigonometric values into $R_y$ and evaluate the arithmetic:
$$R_y = 50 - 40(0.28) - 30(0.96) = 50 - 11.2 - 28.8 = 50 - 40 = 10\text{ N}$$

Combine the two perpendicular components using the Pythagorean theorem ($R = \sqrt{R_x^2 + R_y^2}$):
$$R = \sqrt{30^2 + 10^2} = \sqrt{900 + 100} = \sqrt{1000} \approx 31.6\text{ N}$$

Find the angle $\theta$ above the positive $x$-axis using $\tan\theta = \frac{R_y}{R_x}$:
$$\tan\theta = \frac{10}{30} = \frac{1}{3} \implies \theta = \arctan\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \approx 18.4^\circ$$

hints: If the resultant acts purely in the positive $x$-direction, the net vertical component must be zero ($R_y = 0$).
Set up the vertical resolution equation with $P$ in place of $50\text{ N}$ and solve for $P$.
walkthrough:
Since the resultant acts entirely along the positive $x$-axis, its component in the $y$-direction must equal zero:
$$R_y = P - 40\sin\alpha - 30\cos\alpha = 0$$

Substitute $\sin\alpha = \frac{7}{25}$ and $\cos\alpha = \frac{24}{25}$ to solve for $P$:
$$P = 40\left(\frac{7}{25}\right) + 30\left(\frac{24}{25}\right) = \frac{280 + 720}{25} = \frac{1000}{25} = 40\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
We want the resultant force to act purely along the positive $x$-axis. That means the resultant force in the $y$-direction must equal zero ($R_y = 0$):
$$\sum F_y = 0$$

Write the vertical equilibrium equation with the new upward vertical force $P$:
$$P - 40\sin\alpha - 30\cos\alpha = 0$$

Add the downward terms to both sides to isolate $P$:
$$P = 40\sin\alpha + 30\cos\alpha$$
